//RSZ_CORNERS: 2026-10-09: every resizer step (post-GPL / post-CTS / post-GRT repair, CTS, the post-route ECO) on the gated corners only. With the default (tt, ss, ff) and a 2.0 ns setup margin the resizer chased the ss corner, which no configuration closes at 20 ns (WNS -9 to -10 ns, about 7,600 endpoints): hours of buffering in the tag clusters; on DM_VC4 3400 the post-GRT timing repair alone raised the global-route overflow 66 -> 1,185 and left setup nom_tt -2.67 ns. ss stays reported in the sign-off STA (not gated). The SRAM macro .lib is kept by the first corner read, tt here (STA-1140).
//RUN_POST_GRT_RESIZER_TIMING: 2026-10-09: off for DM_VC4. In every DM_VC4 attempt the global-route overflow exploded in the post-GRT timing repair (66 -> 1,185 with the antenna repair off; 11 -> 9,694 with the resizer on tt / ff, where its hold pass saw 3,808 endpoints, worst -7.8 ns, and inserted 2,746 hold buffers into the congested tag clusters; setup nom_tt then -17.3 ns). Setup after CTS is +2.06 ns at nom_tt; hold is left to the post-route hold ECO on extracted parasitics.
//RT_CLOCK_MIN_LAYER: 2026-10-09: clock nets on met3-met5. Without the post-GRT timing repair the DM_VC4 route was healthy (overflow 22) but the clock skew blew up from placement to global-route parasitics: setup skew 0.870 -> 4.177 ns, hold skew -1.545 -> -5.460 ns (setup nom_tt -0.896, hold -3.902): the clock nets detour through the congested met1 / met2 of the tag clusters. Same fix as the SA2 10.54 mm2 recipe (skew 0.74 -> 2.09 ns there before it).
